title: test_multihop_latency_bounds.py: CUT metrics are the only latency oracle; max<=2*p99 is self-check
description:
## Problem

`python/tests/sim/test_multihop_latency_bounds.py` uses `sim.metrics.latency_stats()` as both the measurement and, in one case, the expected bound. That is the Simulation/Metrics code under test scoring itself.

1. **Sole measurement is CUT telemetry.** Every bound assert reads `stats = sim.metrics.latency_stats()` (e.g. L121, L170, L211, L261, L316, L352, L391, L443). The tests never capture `t_tx = sim.current_time_us` / `t_rx = sim.current_time_us` around TX/RX and assert `t_rx - t_tx` against the budget. If `Metrics.record_reception` stopped recording, recorded 0, or used the wrong clock, these tests would still pass their `<= budget` checks (or skip via `if stats.max_us is not None`).

2. **`test_sustained_load_latency_bounded` (~L407-411) is CUT vs CUT:**
       assert stats.max_us <= 2 * stats.p99_us
   max and p99 are two summaries of the same Metrics sample list. If the CUT inflates every sample by the same factor (including all-10s hops), `max <= 2*p99` still holds. `CATASTROPHIC_LATENCY_US` exists in this file and is not used here.

3. **No airtime floor.** Spec oracle is `lichen.timing.airtime.airtime_us` (SF10/125kHz/CR4-5, spec 09-packets-timing.md). A real hop cannot be faster than airtime, but tests never assert `latency >= airtime_us(len(payload))`. Combined with TX-start polling, measured latency is ~0, which would fail an independent floor.

4. **`LatencyResult` NamedTuple (L71-80) is unused.** It looks like a harness-side result type that was never wired; the tests went to CUT `latency_stats()` instead.

Independent pattern already in `python/tests/sim/test_metrics.py` `test_successful_reception_and_latency`: the test chooses `advance_to(1000)` and asserts `stats.min_us == 1000` — expected value comes from the harness, not from Metrics.

## Why this is not "instrumentation is fine"

Budget constants (300ms/500ms/1s) are independent, but they are applied only to CUT-reported numbers. Without a harness elapsed-time or spec-airtime cross-check, a broken Metrics implementation (always 0, always in-budget, max and p99 scaled together) makes the whole B.5.4 suite green.
design: Independent oracles already in-tree: (1) sim.current_time_us sampled by the test, (2) lichen.timing.airtime.airtime_us per spec/09-packets-timing.md, (3) hardcoded HOP_LATENCY_BUDGET_US / MAX_P99_LATENCY_US / CATASTROPHIC_LATENCY_US. test_metrics.py already asserts min_us == harness advance (1000). Do not derive expected latency from Metrics or from max vs p99 of the same run.
acceptance_criteria: Each latency-bound test records harness timestamps (sim.current_time_us at start_transmission and at successful get_rx_result) and asserts that independent elapsed time, not only sim.metrics.latency_stats(), is within the budget. Floor uses spec airtime (lichen.timing.airtime.airtime_us(payload_len)), not Simulation internals. test_sustained_load_latency_bounded drops or supplements max<=2*p99 with CATASTROPHIC_LATENCY_US / HOP_LATENCY_BUDGET_US. Unused LatencyResult is either wired to those harness samples or removed as part of the same change.
close_reason: Each test records sim.current_time_us around TX/RX and asserts harness elapsed vs Metrics. Floor is lora_medium.airtime_us (spec SF10). LatencyResult wired to harness samples. Sustained-load keeps max<=2*p99 only as a supplement to HOP_BUDGET and CATASTROPHIC.
